claim_1.claim: RNA sequencing analysis of CD4+ CD8+ double-positive T cells from 88 dengue patients showed 20 differentially expressed genes between CD4+ CD8+ DP and CD8+ SP cells, compared to 109 DE genes identified between CD4+CD8+ DP and CD4+ SP T cells, with similar expression profiles in patients with and without plasma leakage.

sources.quote: Overall, there were 20 DE genes (absolute log 2 fold change (FC) > 2, and adjusted p -value (false discovery rate, FDR) < 0.05) identified between CD4 + CD8 + DP and CD8 + SP T cells, compared to 109 DE genes identified between CD4+CD8+ DP and CD4+ SP T cells
CD4 + CD8 + DP T cells isolated from both D+L and D-L groups displayed very similar gene expression profiles and clustered closely to one another based on UMAP analysis.

comparison.finding: 20 differentially expressed genes between CD4+ CD8+ DP and CD8+ SP cells
109 differentially expressed genes between CD4+ CD8+ DP and CD4+ SP cells

claim_2.claim: RNA sequencing analysis of CD4+ CD8+ double-positive T cells between the D+L and D-L groups during the acute febrile phase showed 5 differentially expressed genes.

sources.quote: Only five significant DE genes were identified (Figure 3B,C)

comparison.finding: Only five significant DE genes were identified (Figure 3B,C), which included in D+L group the down-regulated genes DNAJB1 (DnaJ homolog subfamily B member 1), NR4A2 (Nuclear receptor subfamily 4 group A member 2), B3GNT7 (UDP-GlcNAc:betaGal beta-1,3-N-acetylglucosaminyltransferase), and SLC45A1 (Proton-associated sugar transporter A) involved in gene expression and post-translational protein modification as well as the up-regulated gene ABO (Histo-blood group ABO system transferase) gene (Table 4).
